cues.text: Hello. Is this the Triple A Employment agency?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Yes.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Hi. I rang before. My name’s Andrew. Example Andrew Peterson. I rang you earlier and gave you my personal details. If you remember, I’m that student looking for work during the summer holidays.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Oh, sure. Actually, I have your file right here. But... we still need to add some further information.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Yeah, that’s what they told me, and that’s why I’m ringing. What do you need to know?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Well, we have to know your main level of education. It’s a degree, I suppose.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Yes, but I’m still doing it, in engineering. It’s quite interesting. Some of my friends are studying computing though, so I’m interested in that, also.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Well, I’ll just write in your main degree subject. Engineering. We usually have a demand in computing though. Have you worked with computers before?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: No. I just do some programming for fun at the university, but I almost got a job as a computer designer once. Actually, the only job I’ve ever had was as a car salesman, believe it or not.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Well, at least you’ve had experience dealing with customers. What about hobbies though? Sometimes they can help develop useful skills.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Ummm ... in my free time I don’t do much — mostly study. I play chess occasionally at the university chess club. That’s right next to the tennis courts, but I’m not interested in that.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Chess helps develop analytical skills, so I’ll put that down. Of course, it’s your main skills that employers want to know about. What would you say they are?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Well, I’m in my third year now, studying electrical machines and generating systems, but I’d say electronics is my best skill— much better than, say, my machine skills, which aren’t so good, actually.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Okay ... machine skills are in demand, but so too are electronic ones, so we might be able to find you a part-time job in that field. But what sort of money do you expect to got?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Oh, anything really. I’d want the standard payment, let’s say. What’s normal? 1,000 a month? 1,500?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: I’ll just put $1,200, okay?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: That’s fine by me.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: When can you start? Say, within two days?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Easily! Actually, less. In fact, just give me a ring, and I’ll be able to start immediately, although I admit it’ll take me a few days to get used to getting up early in the morning.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Okay! That’s just about it, unless you’d like to add anything else which may help with your application?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Ah, not really. I ride a motorbike, but that’s unimportant. I’m friendly, but every applicant claims that, right? I can speak another language.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Ah, that might be useful, depending on the language. Is it Chinese? A Chinese speaker would go down well.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Spanish, I’m afraid. You see, I grew up with some friends who came from South America.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Okay, I’ll write that down, but I don’t think it will help that much, sorry to say.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Well, thanks for your help, and hopefully I’ll get a job soon, but can I just ask one more question? [Sure] What, basically, are employers looking for when they Interview someone?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Oh, many things. Being hardworking, diligent, and focused on your job is good, but surprisingly, it often means you can’t see the bigger picture, or provide suggestions which help the company move forward. That requires thinking for yourself, outside the box as they say, and being free of the standard ways of approaching tasks. Employers certainly value that.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: I guess experience must help, though?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: It depends. If it involved a routine job, one which didn’t exercise your mind, it might not mean that much at all. But since companies are basically composed of people, it is important to be able to get along with others. There’s no point in hiring someone whom the other employees don’t like, right? That just causes problems — in fact, I would say that being friendly and approachable ranks far more highly than your academic qualifications.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Okay, and that’s all assessed at the interview, right?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Yes, and your qualifications, experience, and approach to the job, such as whether you can do different things, work overtime, or do long hours as needed. But those latter qualities are pretty much standard. What may be more important is based on the fact that things inevitably go wrong. Mistakes are made, and someone’s got to fix them in a way that creates the least disturbance. People with demonstrated abilities to do this are certainly regarded highly.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: I see. That’s very interesting
cues.speaker: Andrew
